title: Updating a copy
goal: Test an upgrade on a copy using a control dataset and rollback plan.
prerequisites: 1c-enterprise.a 5; A1–A2: separate infobase, catalogs, references and documents; synthetic data only.
outcomes: Test an upgrade on a copy using a control dataset and rollback plan.
Record v1 controls and a backup.
sections: A new executable platform version and a new configuration are different changes. Record both versions, compatibility mode and purpose before and after. Do not blame every error on “old 1C” without reproduction. Start with one configuration change on the same platform to avoid mixing two factors.

Begin administration with responsibility boundaries:operators correct input, developers algorithms, and administrators the permitted environment/recovery. Being able to execute a command does not authorize consequences. Record purpose, source, destination and prohibited changes before acting; record outcome and preservation afterwards. This turns potentially dangerous clicks into a controlled experiment with an explicit acceptance condition.

Prepare an old request, a new request, zero duration and rejected input. Reconcile report and references before upgrading. Repeat the same set afterwards and add the new capability’s scenario. Opening the main window is insufficient: lost fields or broken filters may appear only when old data is read.

A full backup restores data, not merely earlier code. Preserve platform/configuration versions, control identities and totals. Restore only to a fresh destination without someone else’s work. File existence is insufficient:open the restored instance and confirm accepted state survives another session. Recovery evidence names what was checked rather than implying every function was covered.

Back up before changing and verify restoration separately. Once an upgrade changes data, replacing the executable alone need not restore earlier state. Keep source and upgraded copies with distinct paths and identities. Preserve failed copies until the cause and safe protocol have been recorded.

Permission tests must allow required work while denying excess. Login failure alone is not an object-permission test. Pair each negative attempt with an allowed control in a suitable environment. Record training limitations separately:one-user login does not prove multi-user separation or authorize production use. Keep credentials out of logs and use synthetic roles/data.

The summary lists passed, failed and untested workflows plus rollback. Untested exchange or permissions do not inherit PASS from unrelated checks. The teaching task delivers a tested candidate rather than publishing it. Real working-system changes require their owner and an agreed maintenance window even after successful tests.

Preserve observations before testing hypotheses. Changing version, role and data together destroys causal explanation. Hand off minimal reproduction and sanitized classification while keeping private logs restricted. Repeat the original case and preservation control after fixing. Record failed attempts before cleanup:they can explain accepted limitations and prevent another unsafe experiment.

lab.title: Test an upgrade on a copy using a control dataset and rollback plan.
lab.environment: Official 1C 8.3.27.x, new training-service-desk copy. Command labels depend on the configuration interface; verify outcomes against data. Training-edition limits are explicit.
steps: Create a separate work copy; record its ID, source ID and platform/configuration build. Never restore over your source.
Record v1 controls and a backup.
Return through another freshly restored instance.
Reopen the copy, repeat the checks and reconcile the unchanged source. Preserve failures separately from the corrected attempt.

v1 controls are restored; upgraded work is not destroyed.

mistakes: Treat an expected value as an observed execution.
Reconcile the result in the specified environment and attach the protocol; the browser model does not execute BSL.
Modify the source infobase while experimenting.
Work on a new copy and verify the source by reopening it separately.
